content:
[42000 Cryptography | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

In this subject, you will delve into the critical role of cryptographic techniques in maintaining data confidentiality and ensuring data integrity. These techniques are foundational in cybersecurity, securing a variety of systems such as wireless networks, online payment systems, and cryptocurrencies. You will explore key principles of cryptography, including both symmetric and asymmetric ciphers, cryptographic hash functions, message authentication codes, and digital signatures. Additionally, this subject introduces you to the popular applications of cryptography, such as the cryptographic designs in blockchain. Through hands-on exercises, you will analyse various cryptographic techniques, use popular cryptographic tools, and practise simulated attacks on cryptographic systems.

[42000 Cryptography | Learning and teaching activities]
The subject will be delivered as a one-hour review and a two-hour laboratory session every week. The learning and lab material are available in Canvas. Students are expected to read the required textbook and study the learning material in their own time before the class.

 The timetabled lecture class will review cryptography theories and designs that students have read about and/or watched videos of prior to coming to class. Students will learn the architectural principles, mathematic theories and key designs of underlying cryptographic algorithms. Students will also learn how to securely use cryptographic algorithms. All material covered is assessable, unless explicitly stipulated otherwise.

 In the labs, students will individually practice cryptographic algorithms and tools to prevent data interception and modification. The lab tasks include various encryption and decryption methods, hashing algorithms, signing messages, and cryptographic tools. In-class guidance and feedback on labs and reports will be provided by tutors.

 Students should form groups for the group implementation project and group research project. Groups should meet up regularly to collaborate, and coordinate efforts on group work in addition to attending scheduled classes. In-class feedback on the group projects will be provided by tutors.

title: Learning outcomes
content:
[42000 Cryptography | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Explain the architectural principles, mathematical theories and key designs of underlying cryptographic algorithms. (D.1)
SLO2: Implement cryptographic techniques and tools to prevent data interception and modification. (D.1)
SLO3: Demonstrate system design principles and programmatic practices that lead to secure software systems. (C.1)
SLO4: Discuss the potential social impact of evolving cryptographic techniques by reviewing recent literature. (B.1)
